hypotheses.reasoning: Origin: events-db reports an open transaction (87799) from enrichment-svc-reconciler, ACTIVE 101 sec, holding a row lock on the events table (#168, ~14:53:55). Its lock blocks enrichment-svc's UPDATE statements, which fail with lock wait timeouts (#176, #189, #192) and statement timeouts at 10s (#187, #194, #200). enrichment-svc then takes ~15s per enrich call, ingest-api times out calling /enrich (#188, #195, #201), its 50-connection pool to enrichment-svc saturates with queued requests (#203, #206, #216), pool checkout times out (#233), and the gateway returns 504s after 12-28s (#199, #204, #210, etc.). The gateway 504s are downstream symptoms and are not cited as root cause. Unrelated items ruled out: the GC pause in event-processor (#182), the DLQ'd malformed message (#183), and the disk warning (#88) do not line up with the onset. The reconciler's lock was never released, so the stuck transaction is the likely cause, though the logs don't show why it hung.

Alternative reading: the enrichment connection pool saturating and queueing requests amplified a modest slowdown into a gateway-wide 504 storm. The pool exhaustion is a symptom here, since the pool only drained because calls hung on the lock, so this is weaker than the lock origin.

verdict.recommendedAction: Identify and kill the stuck enrichment-svc-reconciler transaction (events-db transaction 87799 and any others holding locks on events). Confirm the lock is released, then let the enrichment-svc connection pool drain. Fix the reconciler so its transactions commit or time out promptly. Add a lock-wait or statement timeout on the reconciler path, and shed or retry load at ingest-api while the lock is held. Review the gateway's 504 retry behavior.
